skills.method: Read both installed skills. Drafted from sourced claims, then edited each language in embedded mode for filler, repeated framing, contrast formulas, and natural technical wording. Preserved code-free implementation guidance, attribution, dates, version and availability limits. No first-person testing claims were added.

topics.intent: Developer selection: decide between Browser Use agent/runtime choices and Playwright automation APIs for fixed tests, known steps, exploratory browser work, or managed browser hosting.
topics.distinctFrom: The existing Playwright MCP vs Chrome DevTools MCP guide compares two MCP servers and Chrome diagnostics. This guide compares the Playwright framework/API with Browser Use agent, CLI, library, and browser infrastructure paths; it explicitly distinguishes Playwright MCP from the SDK and Test runner.

publicSignals.title: Browser Use vs Playwright: Which Should You Use?
publicSignals.evidence: Public search surfaced a comparison dated 2026-09-29 with a developer selection framing around explicit repeatable automation versus an AI agent or hosted browser. The page describes itself as research-based and notes that vendor-reported task figures are not a matched independent comparison.
publicSignals.claimScope: Evidence that the exact developer comparison intent is publicly addressed. No read count, search volume, ranking, traffic, or demand magnitude was established. No competitor prose or product facts were reused.

publicSignals.evidence: Public search surfaced a separate comparison focused on architecture and use cases.
publicSignals.claimScope: Evidence of recurring public comparison framing only; not product documentation, a validated benchmark, or quantitative demand.

primarySources.title: Browser Use official repository and README
primarySources.claimScope: Documents the current open-source Python agent, local or cloud browser paths, hosted API, CLI and project integrations. Mutable main branch; no independent performance claim was taken from its benchmark section.

primarySources.title: Browser Use official documentation: Human Quickstart
primarySources.claimScope: Current official open-source quickstart for package installation, browser installation, supported model integrations, and the human-run agent example. The GitHub docs quickstart previously referenced here was stale; it has been replaced. No vendor speed/accuracy marketing claim is reused.

primarySources.title: Browser Use official pyproject.toml
primarySources.claimScope: Current mutable dependency manifest at version 0.13.13. It lists cdp-use and does not list Playwright as a runtime dependency; this is evidence about the current manifest, not proof about every historical release. Browser Use's separate managed browser infrastructure documents Playwright integration.

primarySources.title: Browser Use Developers: Hosted agents and browser infrastructure
primarySources.claimScope: Vendor description of hosted agents, browser infrastructure, Playwright/Puppeteer/CDP integration, and distinct service paths. Prices were not compared because cost depends on service and use.

primarySources.title: Playwright official introduction
primarySources.claimScope: Playwright Test and browser automation framework scope, supported languages and browser engines. Documentation is versioned and can change.

primarySources.title: Playwright official locator guide
primarySources.claimScope: Locator practices and user-facing role/label guidance used in the test selection example.

primarySources.title: Playwright official authentication guide
primarySources.claimScope: Authentication state handling and credential precautions.

primarySources.title: Playwright official website and MCP positioning
primarySources.claimScope: The official website presents Playwright MCP as a separate MCP server option, supporting the article's distinction between the SDK/Test runner and MCP integration.

topics.editorialDecision: Publish as a task-based comparison that disambiguates Browser Use's product paths, separates deterministic test code from agent planning, and distinguishes its current open-source CDP dependency from Playwright support on managed browser infrastructure. Include practical scenarios, session/security boundaries, an evaluation checklist, current documentation links, and no unsupported benchmark or price winner.

primarySources.claimScope: Current product page lists Comet for Mac, Windows, iOS and Android. Platform support does not establish feature parity across devices.

primarySources.title: Perplexity official Ways to Use Comet guide
primarySources.claimScope: Vendor examples of tab references, assistant, actions and browser setup; used to describe documented examples, not guarantee uniform operation.

primarySources.title: Google Gemini Apps Help: Gemini in Chrome availability
primarySources.claimScope: Broader regular Gemini in Chrome eligibility: age 13+ or the applicable age in a user's country, supported region/language, Chromebook Plus/Mac/Windows, latest Chrome, signed-in Chrome, unavailable in Incognito; adult work/school access requires admin enablement. Does not grant Auto Browse eligibility.

primarySources.title: Google Gemini Apps Help: Use Gemini in Chrome
primarySources.claimScope: Current usage instructions, current-tab context, desktop sharing of up to ten open tabs, and opt-in behavior.

primarySources.title: Google Chrome Enterprise Help: Configure Gemini in Chrome
primarySources.claimScope: Enterprise policy and administrator configuration. The article does not claim all Workspace accounts have access.

primarySources.title: Perplexity changelog: Comet now available for everyone
primarySources.claimScope: Perplexity's October 2, 2025 changelog says the base Comet browser was free to download worldwide and identifies concurrent background assistants as a Max-subscriber capability. This establishes free base download at that announcement date and an example of plan-dependent advanced features, not a current full quota/pricing table.

primarySources.title: Google Gemini Apps Help: Auto Browse requirements
primarySources.claimScope: Distinct Auto Browse requirements observed 2026-10-22: age 18+, in the US, English device language, eligible and opted-in Gemini in Chrome, current Chrome, personal Google Account with Google AI Pro or Ultra, Standard or Enhanced Safe Browsing; unavailable in Incognito, when signed into a school account, and in Gemini in Chrome on iPhone/iPad; rollout is gradual. Google says the user reviews a task plan before starting, and the selected sites may receive personal information. Separate from broader regular Gemini in Chrome availability.

primarySources.title: Google Gemini Apps Privacy Hub
primarySources.claimScope: Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, last updated October 19, 2026, includes a specific Gemini in Chrome section. Its notice includes browser page content shared with Gemini Apps among information collected. This is Google's policy statement, not an independent privacy audit.

topics.editorialDecision: Publish a practical named-product comparison. Separate Comet's free-to-download base browser from plan-dependent advanced features, and separate the broader Gemini in Chrome assistant eligibility from Auto Browse's stricter conditions observed 2026-10-22. Include platform support, account-level checks, source-backed privacy guidance, and no invented dollar-price or feature-parity claim.

method.searchMethod: Public web search for current comparison intent followed by direct access to official Browser Use, Playwright, Perplexity and Google documentation. Search-result and page snapshots may vary by account, region, crawl and time.
limitations: Public SERP appearances are discovery evidence only. They are not our query logs, measured search volume, rankings, clicks, or BrowserHub traffic.
No reliable article read counters were present in the selected public comparison evidence; no read totals are claimed.
Official product documentation describes vendor-supported or announced capabilities and can change. It does not establish independent quality, reliability, or identical availability across users.
No software was installed, account was tested, browser task was run, or benchmark was performed for these topics.
No product price winner is claimed. Current price and entitlements should be checked against the reader's actual account and billing location.
